steps.title: Same hardware, a different number in each layer
steps.body:
The i.MX 8M Plus has three SD/MMC controllers. The Boot ROM, U-Boot and Linux each number them differently.

Read one row left to right to see all the names for the same device.

steps.title: uSDHC1 is the Wi-Fi slot
steps.body: At `0x30B4_0000` it is wired to the optional Wi-Fi/BT module (SDIO), is not a boot device and is `mmc0` in Linux. The message `Failed to initialize a non-removable card` is harmless when no Wi-Fi chip is fitted.

steps.title: uSDHC2 is the SD card slot
steps.body: At `0x30B5_0000` on the carrier board. With the boot switch on SD the Boot ROM reads it at 32 KiB; U-Boot calls it `mmc 1` and Linux `/dev/mmcblk1`.

steps.title: Partition 1 becomes /
steps.body: The root filesystem is `mmcblk1p1`, set by `root=/dev/mmcblk1p1`. This repository writes `imx-boot.bin` at the start and an ext4 partition labelled root at 8 MiB.

steps.title: On your PC it is /dev/sdX
steps.body: The numbering `mmcblk1` exists only on the board. On your PC the same card has a name like `/dev/sdX`, so check the device before flashing: the wrong one destroys its data.

steps.title: uSDHC3 is the on-module eMMC
steps.body: At `0x30B6_0000`, 29 GiB on this VAR-SOM, `mmc 2` in U-Boot and `/dev/mmcblk2` in Linux. With the boot switch on eMMC the Boot ROM reads it instead.

steps.anchor: ├ mmcblk2boot0, boot1 (4 MiB each, imx-boot at offset 0)
steps.title: Hardware partitions
steps.body: `boot0` and `boot1` are small hardware boot partitions and `rpmb` is a replay-protected area for secure storage. The Boot ROM reads `imx-boot.bin` from offset 0 of a boot partition when the eMMC is configured to boot from it (`./build.sh uuu emmc` does this); see [chapter 16](../16-booting-from-emmc-with-uuu.md).

steps.anchor: over USB: ./build.sh uuu emmc (docs/16); or user area from SD:
steps.title: Two ways to fill the eMMC
steps.body: Over USB, `./build.sh uuu emmc` writes the user area and the boot partitions and sets the boot configuration. From a board booted from SD, `dd if=sdcard.img of=/dev/mmcblk2 bs=4M` writes the user area only, which boots only while no boot partition is enabled. U-Boot passes `root=/dev/mmcblk2p1` itself. The eMMC is blank today, with no partition table.

steps.title: Takeaway: check the names on the board
steps.body: Use `cat /proc/partitions` or `mmc list` in U-Boot before writing anything, since the same card has three names depending on who is asking.
